tasks.short: Patrol the area, respond promptly to calls and keep the control room informed of status.

steps.what: Officer patrols the specific area by car, bike or on foot
Officer responds promptly to calls for assistance from the control room
Officer radios status updates (en route, arrived, available) to the control room

tasks.design: Status updates are sent with one press on the officer's mobile device to the control room system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) instead of a radio call, freeing the radio for what matters. Patrolling and responding stay fully with the officer; status data are used for dispatch, not to rate officers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every status change was a radio call.
tasks.enabler_now: Police mobile devices and control-room systems support status buttons.
tasks.still_hard: In tense moments officers forget buttons; radio stays the backup.
tasks.human_edge: Getting to the right place fast and reading what is happening on arrival.

reach.learn: Whether status buttons cut radio traffic.

evidence.claim: Control-room systems can take unit status from mobile devices.
Status and location logs that show officers' performance need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from patrol to unit status; incident handling is outside.
Input contract: status codes set by the control room; fallback is radio.
Patrolling and responding do not change.
Status data are not used for performance scores.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Almost all of this task is patrol and response.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Watch traffic and stop drivers, talk with them and check papers, get vehicle data from the plate and complete the fine.

steps.what: Officer monitors traffic to ensure motorists observe traffic regulations and stops unsafe drivers
Officer talks with the driver and checks licence and papers
Officer types the plate and vehicle data into the fine on the handheld
Officer completes the fine with offence and location

tasks.design: The handheld reads the number plate with its camera and fills the vehicle data on the fine from the vehicle register through the police system ({OPS_SYSTEM}), so the officer no longer types them. Watching traffic, talking with drivers and deciding the fine stay with the officer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plate and vehicle data were typed into the handheld.
tasks.enabler_now: Plate reading by phone camera and vehicle register lookups are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Misread plates must be caught; the officer confirms.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a warning or a fine fits the driver in front of you.

reach.learn: Whether plate reading cuts typing errors.

evidence.claim: A municipal scan car checks number plates against the national parking register; an officer checks every photo.
Solely automated decisions with adverse effect need prior human intervention under the police data act.

assumptions: Boundary: from watching traffic to the issued fine; payment is outside.
Input contract: vehicle register lookup through the national police systems; fallback is typing.
Watching, talking and deciding do not change.
The officer confirms every read plate.
research_questions: Do fines with wrong vehicle data fall?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Almost all of this task is on the road.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Get the court day freed, read the summons, find the report and photos, reread them, travel and wait, and testify.

steps.what: Officer reads the summons and the case it concerns
Officer e-mails the planner to free the court day in the roster
Officer searches the archive for the report, notes and photos
Officer rereads the report and notes to prepare to present evidence
Officer travels to and waits at court
Officer testifies in court as a witness in traffic and criminal cases

tasks.design: When a summons is registered, the roster system ({HCM}) blocks the court day automatically and the police registration system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) links the case folder (report, notes, photos) to it, so the officer opens it instead of searching. Rereading, travelling, waiting and testifying stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Court days were arranged by e-mail and case files searched in the archive.
tasks.enabler_now: Roster and registration systems can be linked to court summonses.
tasks.still_hard: Waiting time at court is set by the court's schedule.
tasks.human_edge: Giving clear, honest evidence under cross-examination.

reach.learn: Whether automatic blocks cut last-minute roster changes.

evidence.claim: Roster and registration systems can be linked to court summonses.
Police data on daily tasks are kept at most five years.

assumptions: Boundary: from summons to testimony; the court's decisions are outside.
Input contract: summonses registered by the police court liaison; roster kept by the planner; fallback is e-mail and archive search.
Rereading and testifying do not change.
Planner time is outside the officer's savings.

incremental.description: Officer checks the linked case folder is complete.

approvals.approved_version: The court date from the summons as read by the officer in s2.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is preparation, travel and court time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the incident information, ask the control room for more, see earlier incidents at the address, decide the response with the partner and handle desk complaints.

steps.what: Officer reads the incident information from the control room on the device
Officer radios the control room for more details on the caller and situation
Officer searches for earlier incidents at the address
Officer evaluates complaint and emergency-request information with the partner to determine response requirements
Officer hears complaints at the station desk and decides the follow-up

tasks.design: Updates from the control room (caller details, new information) appear on the officer's device in the incident system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) as they come in, so fewer radio questions are needed, and earlier incidents at the address are shown with each call within the officer's access rights. Deciding the response and handling desk complaints stay with officers; no AI ranks calls or people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Details came by radio and address history needed a separate search.
tasks.enabler_now: Incident systems push updates and linked records to mobile devices.
tasks.still_hard: Address history can bias; it must be read with care and kept within the police data act.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing in the details that this call is more serious than it sounds.

reach.learn: Whether pushed updates shorten radio briefings.

evidence.claim: Incident systems push updates and linked records to officers' devices.
AI that classifies emergency calls or sets dispatch priority is high-risk; this design shows records only.
A crime forecasting system was phased out after an evaluation; predictive scores are not used here.

assumptions: Boundary: from the incoming call to the response decision; the response itself is outside.
Input contract: incident updates entered by control room operators; address history from the registration system within access rights; fallback is radio.
Deciding and desk complaints do not change.
research_questions: Does radio traffic per incident fall?

incremental.description: Officer reads pushed updates while en route as partner.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is judgement with the partner and at the desk.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The patrol officer keeps patrol, traffic work, testimony and every decision; radio calls, typing and searches shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An officer who arrives at every call knowing what the system knows and spends the shift on the street.
